$comment: Per-file counts of raw palette tokens read in foreground position, as they
stood when the ratchet landed (YaleSites-Internal#1632). See
foreground-purity.mjs for what counts and why some paths are exempt.
These may only ever go DOWN. foreground-purity.test.mjs fails if a file
exceeds its count, if a file not listed here has any at all, if a listed
file is now clean (delete the entry), or if a count is padded above what is
really there. Raising a number to make a red build green is not a fix.
Converting these to the surface contract is Phase 2 (#1631), component by
component. Regenerate the real counts with:
node components/00-tokens/colors/foreground-purity.mjs
ONE count has been raised rather than lowered, which this file otherwise
forbids: _yds-publication-detail.scss went 2 -> 3 in
YaleSites-Internal#1662. That chip paints its own --color-gray-100
background and previously set no colour at all, so its plain-text items
inherited the component root. Moving that root onto the section contract
sent the section's foreground onto a chip that stayed gray-100 -- below AA
on 21 of 42 pairings, worst 1.07:1. The third entry is the paired
foreground that closes it (--color-basic-brown-gray, 4.54:1, the value the
chip already inherited, so rendering is unchanged).
That is a raw palette foreground the ratchet must count, but it is the
CORRECT kind: a rule that paints a background pairing its own foreground,
the same category as .event-meta__multiple-dates already in this file. It
is not a suppressed defect, which is what the may-only-fall rule exists to
prevent.
A SECOND count has been raised for the same reason: taxonomy-display's
`default` dial went 1 -> 5 in YaleSites-Internal#1641. That dial paints its
own --color-gray-100 box and set no link colour at all, so
.taxonomy-display__link inherited --color-link-base from whichever
ancestor last set it -- the enclosing themed SECTION on 3 of 6 section
themes, which sets it to white for its own background, not this box's.
White-on-near-white measured 1.07:1 on 21 of 42 (section theme x global
theme) pairings. The four new entries pin --color-link-base/-hover and
--color-link-visited-base/-hover to the same raw palette values
tokens.css already sets at :root (blue-medium, gray-700, purple-visited,
purple-visited-hover) -- unchanged outside a themed section, and closes
the leak inside one because a directly-matching declaration beats an
inherited one.
The calendar's count (10) is UNCHANGED but the decision behind leaving it
is recorded here rather than nowhere, per YaleSites-Internal#1641's second
acceptance criterion (audit the Events Calendar block against every
section background, or record why it needs none). It is not recorded in
surface-contract-baseline.json's out_of_scope section, the usual home for
this kind of decision, because that section is scoped to components
`surface-contract.mjs` actually detects -- ones that paint a background
inside a `[data-component-theme]` block. _yds-calendar.scss has no such
block at all (grep for data-component-theme/data-section-theme/
color-section-foreground across the whole components/03-organisms/
calendar/ directory returns nothing); adding it there was tried and
broke two surface-contract.test.mjs assertions (a file listed as
out_of_scope must actually paint a themed background, or it is flagged
as a stale entry) for no gain, since the file was reverted.
The decision: NOT fixed, deferred rather than unnecessary. The block is
not editor-placeable -- grepping every
web/profiles/custom/yalesites_profile/config/sync/user.role.*.yml in the
yalesites-project checkout finds no role granting 'create event_calendar
block content', and of the two roles with blanket block admin
permissions ('administer block content' / 'administer block types' /
'administer blocks'), only platform_admin has any of the three --
site_admin, the highest role a site's own editorial team holds, has
none. It paints only raw palette tokens (--color-basic-black on
.calendar__day, --color-blue-yale on .calendar-event__type, plus
--color-gray-* elsewhere) and is not aware of section theming at all.
Measured against all 6 section backgrounds x 7 global themes (42
pairings) via contrast-ratio.mjs: .calendar__day fails AA on 19/42,
.calendar-event__type on 23/42 (union of both: 23/42). That is the risk
if a platform admin ever places one inside a themed section; fixing it
would be a large, unreviewed visual change to a component no editor can
reach, so it is left for a follow-up rather than done here.
